# New renderings — odyssey-117 (Odyssey 24.214–326)

Rows in the table format of `conventions.md` (Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose). Lines that already stand in a published part, and words already fixed by an existing row, are not repeated here.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἀλωή (24.221, 24.224, 24.226; the whole planted ground of Laertes, with trees, vines and beds) | "plot" | "plot" | "orchard" (kept for ὄρχατος, and shipped for ἀλωή at 6.293), "vineyard" (7.122; "vineyard plot" for ἀλωῆς οἰνοπέδοιο), "farm" (ἀγρός), "estate" (τέμενος); the note says the word is a planted plot |
| ἐϋκτιμένη ἀλωή (24.226) | "the well-built plot" | "the well-tilled plot" (+ note: ἐϋκτιμένη is the adjective of houses and towns) | "well-settled" (the sense given for the island at 9.130), "well-founded", "well-ordered"; `l` keeps "well-built" as for ἐϋκτίμενον δόμον (24.214) |
| λιστρεύω (24.227) · ἀμφιλαχαίνω (24.242) | "digging round" · "was digging round" | "digging around" · "went on digging round" | "hoeing", "weeding" (each fixes a tool or a task); λιστρεύω is related to λίστρον "shovel" |
| ῥαπτός (24.228, 24.229, of the tunic and the leg-guards) | "stitched" | "patched" (tunic) / "stitched" (leg-guards) | "sewn", "ragged" (reserved for ῥωγαλέος), "mended" |
| κνημῖδες βοείαι (24.228–229) | "oxhide greaves" | "oxhide leg-guards" | "gaiters", "leggings", "boots"; κνημῖς is the word behind ἐυκνήμιδες "well-greaved", so `l` keeps "greaves", and `i` says "leg-guards" because these are leather and not a warrior's bronze |
| γραπτῦς (24.229, γραπτῦς ἀλεείνων; rare noun, sense taken from γράφω "scratch") | "scratches" | "scratches" | "thorns", "pricks", "the briars" |
| χειρῖδες (24.230) | "gloves" | "gloves" | "gauntlets" (armour), "mittens", "hand-guards" |
| αἰγείη κυνέη (24.231, a farmer's cap of hide; follows the table's κυνέη "helmet") | "a goatskin helmet" | "a goatskin cap" (+ note: κυνέη is the soldier's helmet-word) | "goatskin hat", "hood", "helm"; `l` keeps "helmet" as for κυνέη, and `i` gives the thing. `i` "cap" departs from the row for κυνέη (22.102 etc.), which lists "cap" as avoided; that row concerns armour, and here the goatskin κυνέη of a working farmer is a cap, as the note says (every shipped κυνέη is "helmet") |
| πένθος ἀέξων (24.231) | "increasing his grief" | "adding to his grief" | "nursing", "feeding", "making his sorrow grow" (the participle is ἀέξω "make grow", and "increase" keeps that) |
| τὸν δὲ παριστάμενος προσεφώνεε φαίδιμος υἱός (whole-line speech introduction, 24.243; "the glorious son" is Odysseus) | "And to him, standing beside him, spoke the glorious son:" | "His glorious son stood beside him and spoke to him:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο), "addressed" (reserved for προσέειπε / προσέφη); φαίδιμος keeps "glorious" and υἱός "son", with no name supplied, as in the row for 16.308 |
| ἀδαημονίη (24.244; ἀδαήμων "unacquainted", 17.283) | "inexperience" | "you are not unskilled" (in the sentence) | "ignorance" (reserved for the root of ἀγνοιέω "fail to know"), "stupidity" |
| κομιδή (24.245, 24.247, 24.249; the noun of κομίζω "care for") | "care" | "care" | "tending", "attention", "husbandry", "upkeep" |
| αὐχμέω (24.250, αὐχμεῖς) | "to be unkempt" | "to be unkempt" | "to be dry" (the root-sense, given in the note), "dirty", "filthy" (kept for ῥυπόων), "squalid" (kept for ἀϋσταλέος in `i`); `l` shares "unkempt" with ἀϋσταλέος, two Greek words with one English |
| ἀεργίη (24.251) | "idleness" | "idleness" | "laziness", "sloth", "neglect" |
| δούλειος (24.252, of a look) | "slavish" | "slavish" | "servile", "menial", "of a slave" |
| εἶδος καὶ μέγεθος (24.253, accusatives of respect) | "form and size" | "form and size" | "looks and stature" (φυή and μῆκος keep "stature" and "height"), "appearance and height" |
| βασιλῆϊ ἀνδρὶ ἔοικας (24.253) | "you are like a kingly man" | "you look like a kingly man" | "like a king" (drops ἀνδρί), "royal", "of royal bearing" |
| εὑδέμεναι μαλακῶς (24.255) | "to sleep softly" | "should sleep softly" | "sleep gently", "sleep comfortably", "on a soft bed" (μαλακῶς is an adverb and supplies no noun) |
| δίκη ἐστὶ γερόντων (24.255) | "this is the way of old men" | "that is the way of old men" | "the right of old men", "the justice", "the custom" (reserved for θέμις); follows the shipped "the way of servants", "the way of mortals" and "the way of the gods" (odyssey-066, -053, -092) |
| ἀρτίφρων (24.261; ἄρτιος + φρήν) | "apt-minded" | "of sound judgement" (οὔ τι μάλ’ ἀρτίφρων "none too sound of judgement") | "sound-minded" (reserved for ἐχέφρων), "prudent" (πεπνυμένος), "sensible", "right-minded"; the other "-minded" epithets are taken |
| ἀμφὶ ξείνῳ ἐμῷ (24.263) | "about my guest-friend" | "about my guest-friend" | "stranger" (reserved for address), "friend", "host"; follows the table's ξεῖνος "guest-friend" |
| πατρίδι γαίῃ (24.266, with φίλῃ) | "my dear fatherland" | "my own dear land" | "my native soil"; follows the table's φίλη πατρὶς αἶα and πατρίδα γαῖαν "fatherland" |
| γένος εὔχετο ἔμμεναι (24.269) · ἔφασκε (iterative) | "his birth he declared to be" · "he said" | "declared that he was Ithacan by birth" · "kept saying" | "claimed" (the table's εὔχομαι is "declare"), "boasted" |
| χρυσοῦ … ἑπτὰ τάλαντα (24.274) | "seven talents of gold" | "seven talents of well-made gold" | "seven bars of gold", "seven ingots"; τάλαντον is a weight, kept as "talent" |
| κρητὴρ πανάργυρος ἀνθεμόεις (24.275) | "a mixing-bowl all of silver, flowery" | "a mixing-bowl all of silver and decorated with flowers" | "silver-plated", "embossed", "blossoming", "wholly silver"; πανάργυρος follows the table's πάγχαλκος "all of bronze", ἀνθεμόεις is "flowery" (cf. ἄνθινον εἶδαρ "flowery food") |
| ἁπλοΐς χλαῖνα (24.276) | "single cloak" | "single cloak" | "plain", "simple", "unlined", "thin"; ἁπλοΐς is "of one fold", the opposite of the table's δίπλαξ "double cloak" |
| φάρεα καλά (24.277) | "fine cloaks" | "fine cloaks" | "robes", "mantles" (both turned down at 3.467 for φᾶρος); the English "cloak" is shared with χλαῖνα in the same list, two Greek words with one English, and the note says they are different garments |
| εἰδαλίμη (24.279; rare, from εἶδος "looks") | "comely" | "comely" | "handsome", "shapely", "well-favoured", "lovely" (reserved for ἐρατεινός / ἐραννός) |
| ἀμύμονα ἔργα ἰδυῖα (24.278; of women) | "knowing blameless works" | "skilled in blameless crafts" | "flawless", "faultless", "perfect"; follows the table's ἀμύμων "blameless" (+ note: meaning not known) and κεδνὰ ἰδυῖα "knowing" |
| τὸν δ’ ἠμείβετ’ ἔπειτα πατὴρ κατὰ δάκρυον εἴβων (whole-line reply-formula, 24.280; the father is Laertes) | "Him then answered his father, a tear letting fall:" | "Then his father, letting a tear fall, answered him:" | "weeping" (drops εἴβω), "shedding" (reserved for χέων), "pouring" (λείβων); κατὰ δάκρυον εἴβων keeps the shipped "letting fall" (11.391, where it is "abundant tear" for θαλερὸν δάκρυον; here without θαλερόν), and "tear" is singular in `l` |
| ἦ τοι μὲν γαῖαν ἱκάνεις (24.281) | "truly indeed you have come to the country" | "you have indeed reached the country" | "land" (reserved for δῆμος), "earth", "soil"; follows the table's γαῖα "country" |
| δῶρα ἐτώσια χαρίζεο (24.283) | "gifts in vain you were giving freely" | "it was in vain that you gave these gifts so freely" | "gifts to no purpose", "gifts that you made useless" (the verb is not θῆκεν, 22.256); χαρίζομαι is "give freely", not "favour" |
| ὀπάζων (24.283, μυρί’ ὀπάζων) | "bestowing" | "bestowing" | "heaping", "adding", "accompanying" |
| ἀμειψάμενος δώροισιν (24.285) | "having requited you with gifts" | "would have repaid you … with gifts" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο), "exchanged", "rewarded" |
| ξενίῃ ἀγαθῇ (24.286) | "with good hospitality" | "with good hospitality" | "generous hospitality", "kindly welcome"; ξενίη follows the table's "hospitality" (ξενίη τράπεζα) |
| ἡ γὰρ θέμις, ὅς τις ὑπάρξῃ (24.286) | "for that is the custom, for whoever may begin" | "for that is the custom whenever someone has made the first move" | "right" (avoided for θέμις), "the law", "the rule"; follows the table's θέμις "custom" |
| πόστον ἔτος ἐστίν, ὅτε … (24.288) | "which year in number is it, when …" | "how many years ago was it that …" | "how long has it been since", "in what year"; πόστος is the ordinal "which in number" |
| ὅν που τῆλε φίλων καὶ πατρίδος αἴης (24.290; construction broken off) | "whom, I suppose, far from his dear ones and from his fatherland" | "Far from his dear ones and his fatherland, I suppose" | "perhaps", "doubtless"; που is "I suppose", and the relative ὅν is not carried into `i` |
| περιστείλασα (24.293) | "having laid him out" | "after laying him out" | "having wrapped", "having dressed", "having shrouded" (each picks one act) |
| πολύδωρος (24.294, ἄλοχος πολύδωρος) | "rich in gifts" | "rich in gifts" (+ note: whether she brought many gifts or many were given for her is not said) | "richly dowered", "of many gifts", "much-given"; built like πολύχρυσος "rich in gold" |
| ὀφθαλμοὺς καθελοῦσα (24.296) | "having closed his eyes" | "closing his eyes" | "having drawn down his lids"; follows the table's χερσὶ κατ’ ὀφθαλμοὺς ἑλέειν "to close my eyes" |
| ἐν λεχέεσσιν (24.295, plural for one bed, said of the bed of the dead) | "on the bed" | "on the bed" | "on the bier" (silently picks the sense), "in the beds" |
| ἔμπορος (24.300) | "passenger" | "passenger" | no change; follows the shipped ἔμπορος "passenger" (2.318); listed because the second half of the line, νηὸς ἐπ’ ἀλλοτρίης, explains the word |
| τοιγὰρ ἐγώ τοι πάντα μάλ’ ἀτρεκέως καταλέξω (24.303) | "Well then, I to you everything very exactly will recount." | "Well then, I will tell you everything quite exactly." | "Therefore", "So then" (drop the answering force of τοιγάρ), "truly" (reserved for ἐτήτυμον); καταλέξω keeps the verb of the table's ἀτρεκέως κατάλεξον "recount it exactly" |
| Ἀλύβας · Ἀφείδας · Πολυπήμων · Ἐπήριτος · Σικανίη (24.304–307; names of Odysseus' invented story) | Alybas · Apheidas · Polypemon · Eperitus · Sicania | same | "Alybantes", "Apheides", "Polypemonides" (the patronymic is "Polypemon's son"), "Eperitos"; the familiar Latinised forms, as for the other names in the table |
| πλάζω, aorist active (24.307, πλάγξ’ … με δαίμων) | "drove me astray" | "drove me off course" | "made me roam" (kept for the passive in i, "roamed"), "wandered" (reserved for ἀλάομαι); the passive πλάγχθη 1.2 stays "was driven astray" |
| μίξεσθαι ξενίῃ ἠδ’ ἀγλαὰ δῶρα διδώσειν (24.314) | "to meet in hospitality and to give splendid gifts" | "that we should meet as host and guest and give splendid gifts" | "to be joined in friendship" (the bond, ξενία, is a hospitality tie), "to exchange gifts" alone (drops μίξεσθαι); μίγνυμι keeps "mingle, join", "splendid" as for ἀγλαός |
| ἄχεος νεφέλη μέλαινα (24.315; "a cloud of grief") | "a cloud of grief … dark" | "a dark cloud of grief" | "black cloud" (μέλας "black" is kept for ships, night and death), "gloomy", "sable"; "dark" as for the wine, the water, the wave and the earth |
| κόνις αἰθαλόεσσα (24.316) | "sooty dust" | "sooty dust" | "ashes" (the Greek says dust, as the note explains), "black dust", "smoky dust"; follows the table's αἰθαλόεις "sooty" |
| χεύατο κὰκ κεφαλῆς πολιῆς (24.317) | "poured it down from over his grey head" | "poured it down over his grey head" | "scattered", "sprinkled" (the verb is χέω "pour"); πολιός keeps the table's "grey" |
| ἁδινὰ στεναχίζων (24.317) | "groaning heavily" | "groaning heavily" | "groaning thickly", "loudly", "bitterly"; follows the table's ἁδινὸν γοόωσα "sobbing heavily" |
| δριμὺ μένος (24.319; δριμύς "sharp, pungent", of the rush of feeling before tears) | "a sharp strength" | "a sharp surge of feeling" (+ note) | "bitter", "acrid", "sharp spirit" (θυμός is "heart" and "spirit" is reserved for θυμὸς ἀγήνωρ); μένος keeps "strength" in `l`, as in the table |
| τοῦ δ’ ὠρίνετο θυμός (24.318) | "his heart was stirred" | "his heart was stirred" | "his spirit was moved" (θυμός is "heart"), "his heart was roused" |
| κύσσε δέ μιν περιφὺς ἐπιάλμενος, ἠδὲ προσηύδα (whole-line, 24.320) | "He kissed him, having clung round him, having leapt upon him, and spoke to him:" | "He sprang upon him, threw his arms around him, kissed him, and spoke to him:" | "embraced" for κύσσε (it is "kissed"), "addressed" (reserved for προσέειπε / προσέφη); περιφύς keeps the sense of περιφῦναι at 24.236 (`l` "cling round") and the shipped "clung round" for the same verb (odyssey-077, odyssey-096); `i` gives the act, "threw his arms around" |
| κεῖνος μέν τοι ὅδ’ αὐτὸς ἐγώ, πάτερ, ὃν σὺ μεταλλᾷς (24.321) | "That man, truly, here himself am I, father, whom you inquire after," | "I am that very man, father, whom you are asking after;" | "I am he" (loses κεῖνος and αὐτός), "Here I am, the one you seek"; μεταλλάω keeps the shipped "inquire" (3.231) |
| ἴσχεο κλαυθμοῖο γόοιό τε δακρυόεντος (24.323) | "hold yourself back from weeping and from tearful lament" | "keep yourself from weeping and tearful lament" | "stop crying", "cease from lamentation", "tear-filled"; γόος keeps "lament" |
| μάλα δὲ χρὴ σπευδέμεν ἔμπης (24.324) | "and very much is it necessary to hasten all the same" | "but there is great need to hurry all the same" | "we must hurry nonetheless", "we cannot wait" (drop χρή or ἔμπης); ἔμπης is "all the same" |
| λώβην τινύμενος θυμαλγέα καὶ κακὰ ἔργα (24.326) | "taking vengeance for heart-paining insult and evil deeds" | "taking vengeance for the insult that pained my heart and for their evil deeds" | "outrage" for λώβη with θυμαλγής (the shipped practice for λώβη with θυμαλγής is "insult", odyssey-091 and -100; "outrage" stays for the plain noun, odyssey-095 and -099); follows the shipped "heart-paining insult" / "insult that pained the heart" |
